I farm here in Mangochi on my small piece of land, and maize is what feeds my family. Fertilizer prices are very high these days, but I try to get a little through the government subsidy program if my name comes up — otherwise I use the manure from my goats and chickens to help the soil. I plant hybrid seed when I can afford it because it gives more grain, and I intercrop with pigeon peas to help the soil and have something else to eat. I do not have a pump or river nearby, so I depend on the rains, and my wife and older children help me with the weeding and harvesting.
